chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Regarding a mukatab (slave who has agreed to pay a fixed sum for his freedom) who pays half of his manumission contract and the other half remains due, so he calls his masters and says, 'Take what remains in one lump sum.' He said: They take what remains and he is freed. This does not contradict the first report because it only included the permissibility of taking his money from the installments (al-nujum), and did not include the obligation of that upon him. And the first report included that it is for him to refuse from that, and there is no contradiction or opposition between them on this basis.

key_terms.إِبَاحَة: Permissibility: The legal status of allowing an action without obligating it.
key_terms.النُّجُوم: Al-Nujum: The installments or scheduled payments agreed upon in the manumission contract.
key_terms.تَنَافٍ: Contradiction/Incompatibility: The state where two legal rulings cannot coexist.
key_terms.مُكَاتَب: Mukatab: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom.
key_terms.وُجُوب: Obligation: The legal status requiring an action to be performed.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mukatab pays half his manumission debt and offers to pay the rest in one lump sum?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs the principle of reconciling apparent contradictions (jam' bayn al-khabarayn) by distinguishing between permissibility (ibaha) and obligation (wujub), clarifying that the master may accept the lump sum but is not compelled to do so. This ruling preserves the mukatab's autonomy in debt settlement, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on facilitating manumission while respecting contractual flexibility. The resolution underscores the nuanced approach of the Imams in harmonizing seemingly conflicting narrations through precise legal categorization.
